guarantees.claim: message_length_d defaults to the current message_length.
When hash_start is active, message_length_d is forced to all zeros, overriding any CSR write or message-write increment.
When hash_start is inactive and msg_write, sha_en, packer_ready are all active, message_length_d is set to message_length plus wmask_ones sign-extended to 64 bits, overriding CSR writes.
guarantees.cond: !hash_start and msg_write and sha_en and packer_ready

guarantees.claim: When hash_start is inactive and the message-write condition is false, the lower 32 bits of message_length_d can be updated from reg2hw.msg_length_lower.q if its qe is set, and the upper 32 bits from reg2hw.msg_length_upper.q if its qe is set. These updates occur on top of the default message_length value and can happen simultaneously.

assumptions.claim: wmask_ones correctly encodes the number of bytes written in the current cycle (e.g., the popcount of a write byte-enable).
assumptions.cond: when msg_write, sha_en, packer_ready are active (increment path)
assumptions.risk: If wmask_ones is inaccurate, the message length counter will be corrupted, leading to incorrect HMAC tag computation or length-related attacks.

assumptions.claim: msg_write, sha_en, and packer_ready are mutually coherent and only asserted when a valid data word is being written and the HMAC engine is ready.
assumptions.cond: any cycle where the increment path may fire
assumptions.risk: Spurious or incorrect assertions could cause erroneous length updates or missed counts.

assumptions.claim: CSR writes to msg_length_lower/upper are only performed when the HMAC is idle (i.e., hash_start and the message-write condition are both false), so the stable CSR update window is respected.
assumptions.cond: when the chunk is not updating length via hash_start or msg_write
assumptions.risk: If a CSR write occurs simultaneously with a message write or near a hash_start, the length could be corrupted or an intermediate mixed value could be latched.

assumptions.claim: hash_start is asserted only at the very beginning of a new hash operation and is deasserted before any msg_write can occur, so the zeroing of message_length_d does not interfere with active counting.
assumptions.risk: If hash_start is pulsed during a message stream, the length counter would reset and subsequent increments would be off, breaking HMAC integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: The definition of wmask_ones is not in this chunk. It must equal the exact byte count of the write data. If generated from a write strobe or byte mask, its width and encoding must be verified to match the 64-bit addition.
uncertain_points.cond: whenever the increment path is taken
uncertain_points.risk: Mismatch could cause cumulative length error, leading to wrong HMAC tag.

uncertain_points.claim: The chunk's guard_context lists 'generate if: reg2hw.msg_length_lower.qe' and 'generate if: reg2hw.msg_length_upper.qe', which are run-time signals, not compile-time constants. This may be a tool artifact or indicate a mis-captured generate condition. If real, it would mean this block only exists when those qe signals are statically true, making the internal if checks redundant.
uncertain_points.risk: Could lead to confusion about whether the CSR update path is always available in all configurations; misuse could break length programming.
